page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine tailored for graphics, machine learning inference, and media workloads. The server features an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16 GB of system RAM. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. The instance includes no bundled local storage and requires attached network block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight an intentional architectural focus on hardware acceleration rather than host compute. Host CPU and memory throughput tests consistently place in the bottom 25%, with Geekbench multi-core at 2294.0 and multi-threaded decompression at 14.93 GB/sec. In contrast, GPU acceleration demonstrates top-tier capability, ranking in the top 10% for large language model inference. The platform achieves 2,296.42 tokens per second for prompt processing and 52.18 tokens per second for generation on 7B parameter models.

The primary tradeoff of the g2-standard-4 is the stark contrast between host computing capacity and GPU throughput. Because host memory is constrained to 16 GB and general compute metrics are modest, it offers high cost efficiency strictly when tasks offload intensive computation directly to the NVIDIA L4 accelerator. Deploying CPU-heavy or high-memory data processing tasks on this instance leads to underutilized accelerator costs.

The instance is best suited for small to medium deep learning inference, AI-driven video transcoding, real-time graphics rendering, and microservice-level machine learning deployments that fit within the 24 GB GPU memory boundary.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for inference and media workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 4 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs across 2 physical cores at 2.2 GHz and 16 GB of system memory, paired with a single 24 GB NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network storage for persistent data. While host CPU benchmarks and memory bandwidth consistently place in the bottom 25%, the integrated GPU delivers top-tier performance, processing prompt workloads on 7B parameter models at over 2,290 tokens per second. The server provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for tasks that offload work directly to the accelerator, making it optimal for model serving, image synthesis, video transcoding, and small-to-medium deep learning inference pipelines.

bullet_points: 1 NVIDIA L4 GPU (Ada Lovelace architecture) with 24 GB VRAM
4 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs (2 physical cores at 2.2 GHz)
16 GB system memory (4 GB per vCPU)
